full_judgment: 13. Arguing the case in respect of appellant No. 1 Rattan Kha, Mr. Malek submits that the Intern by which the appellant No. 1 was allegedly recognised by P.W. 1 has neither been seized nor exhibited at the trial. The assertion by P.W. 1 that there was a burning lantern in the ground floor and that it was taken to the first floor by the dacoits the selves has not been challenged by the defence. When the assertion of P.W. 1 remains unchallenged there is no further burden of proof. Mr. Malek further submits that as the informant P.W. 1 did not disclose the recognition of appellant Rattan Kha to the inmates of the house, namely, P.Ws. 2-5, the story of recognition of Rattan Kha by P.W. 1 should be disbelieved. P.W. 2 was aged 18 and P.W. 3 was aged 14 at the time of trial. P.W. 4 and P.W. 5 were victims of separate and simultaneous dacoitics themselves. They were all waiting for the arrival of outsiders for help and solace. As soon as the outsiders arrived at the scene P.W. 1 disclosed about the recognition of appellant No. 1. P.W. 6 Belayet Hossain amply corroborates P.W. 1 on recognition. There is no reason why P.W. 6 should be disbelieved because he is a disinterested witness.
